page.overview:
Who is Tevildo?

Tevildo-meoita, also known as Tiberth and the Prince of Cats, was believed to be the mightiest of all cats, being "an evil fay in beastlike shape" according to "The Tale of Tinúviel" in . Being a demonic servant of Melko, his character eventually became Sauron while they were treated as separate characters in Beren and Lúthien.

In addition to his might and massive size, Tevildo was gifted a mystical collar made of gold by Melko, which enhanced the size of his cat-servants and held his hill-top castle together. He dwelled within a castle on a cliff "not utterly distant" from Angamandi. He was also said to harbor a few mice that were as fierce and large as rats which he allowed to dwell in dark holes "for his own private sport and suffered not their numbers to dwindle". While his subjects feared the dogs that dwelled in the woods nearby, he had a particular scorn for Huan, the Captain of Dogs, for Huan once tasted his fur even as Tevildo-meoita paid him for it with a gash from his great claws. Tevildo would have died had he not been saved by an Orc-host that heard his cries. Tevildo-meoita remained prideful and wished to do harm to Huan in revenge.

In the Quest for the Silmaril, Beren was captured by Melko and was sent to work as a thrall catching birds and beasts in Tevildo-meoita’s kitchens. Upon meeting Beren for the first time, Tevildo-meoita took an instant disliking of him due to smelling that he preferred dogs over cats. He also initially assumed that Melko sent Beren for the cats "to make meat of him". When Melko’s intent was made clear, Tevildo-meoita boasted in scorn that no race was better at catching birds and beasts than his subjects. However, despite this, Tevildo-meoita gave Beren a difficult test to prove his skill as a thrall, tasking him to catch three fierce mice within three days. Beren failed and attained nothing more than a bitten finger. When Tevildo-meoita was made aware of Beren’s failure, he had him punished with a few scratches and made him a scullion. So miserable did Tevildo-meoita make Beren that he wished he never saw Tinúviel.
